```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
# Add any other libraries here
library(dplyr)
library(tidymodels)


```


```{r load-data1}
# load your data 
getwd()

hd_mortalitybyca<- read.csv("data/hd_mortalitybyca.csv")

```

```{r load-data2}
# 1. one year, all ages, both sexes 
hd_total2015 <- hd_mortalitybyca %>% 
  filter(Year == 2015, 
         AgeGroup == "All Ages", 
         Sex == "All",
         Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease") 

# 2. National rate  (Scotland total row) 
scotland_rate <- hd_total2015 %>% 
  filter(Ca == "S92000003") %>% 
  pull(CrudeRate) 

# 3.  above/below national 
hd_councils <- hd_total2015 %>% 
  filter(Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease", Ca != "S92000003") %>%
  mutate(national_rate = scotland_rate,
         difference = CrudeRate - national_rate, 
         status = if_else(CrudeRate > national_rate, "Above national", "Below national")) 

council_area_rate <- hd_councils %>% 
  select(national_rate, CrudeRate, difference, status, Ca, EASR) 

view(council_area_rate) 

```
```

```
```{r}
ggplot(council_area_rate, aes(x = difference)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 15,
    fill = "skyblue",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    colour = "red",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  labs (
    title = "DIstribution of Differences",
    x = "Difference from National Rate",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
- Each bar counts how many councils fall within a 10-point band of difference from the Scotland-wide rate.
- The red dashed line at 0 is the national rate. Councils to the left of it are below the national rate, and councils to the right are above it.
- It's a quick way to see whether most councils sit near the national rate or spread widely around it, and whether the distribution is lopsided.

From the histogram we can see...

```{r}
rate_hd <- hd_mortalitybyca %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(2015, 2023),
         AgeGroup == "All Ages", Sex == "All",
         Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease",
         Ca != "S92000003") %>%
  select(Ca, Year, CrudeRate)


council_order <- rate_hd %>%
  filter(Year == 2023) %>%
  arrange(CrudeRate) %>%
  pull(Ca)

rate_hd <- rate_hd %>%
  mutate(Ca = factor(Ca, levels = council_order))

ggplot(rate_hd, aes(x = CrudeRate, y = Ca)) +
  geom_col(fill = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ Year) +
  labs(title = "CHD death rate by council area, 2015 and 2023",
       x = "Crude Rate", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}


spread_hd <- hd_mortalitybyca %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(str_remove(Year, "p"))) %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(2015, 2023),
         AgeGroup == "All Ages", Sex == "All",
         Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease",
         Ca != "S92000003") %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    highest = max(CrudeRate),
    lowest  = min(CrudeRate),
    range   = highest - lowest,
    sd      = sd(CrudeRate),
    ratio   = highest / lowest,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

spread_hd %>% mutate(across(-Year, ~ round(.x, 1)))

view(spread_hd)
```
